question: What is the primary aim of musculoskeletal rehabilitation?
explanation: Musculoskeletal rehabilitation aims primarily to restore lost physical function and reduce pain in clients with impaired mobility. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h1)

question: Prolonged immobility after a bone fracture leads to which major physical complication?
explanation: Lack of movement causes muscles to waste away and joints to lose their full range of motion. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h1)

question: Short-term rehabilitation goals typically focus on which outcome?
explanation: Short-term goals target immediate priorities like pain control and preventing early complications of immobility. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h2)

question: Why is involving the client in setting rehabilitation goals important?

options.B: It increases motivation and compliance with exercises
options.C: It shortens the hospital stay automatically
options.D: It reduces the need for nursing documentation

explanation: Clients who take part in planning their recovery are more likely to commit to their prescribed therapy routines. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which tool is commonly used to grade muscle strength during a physical assessment?
explanation: Manual muscle testing provides a standardized numerical grade from zero to five for muscle power. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why is assessing nutritional status important during musculoskeletal recovery?

options.A: Food intake prevents all forms of surgical infection
options.B: Good nutrition eliminates the need for physical therapy
options.C: Protein and calcium are essential for tissue healing
options.D: Calories stop joint stiffness from developing

explanation: Adequate nutritional building blocks are necessary for bone remodeling and muscle repair processes. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of passive range of motion exercises?

options.D: Replacing the need for active walking

explanation: Passive exercises keep joints flexible and prevent shortening of soft tissues when clients cannot move themselves. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h4)

question: A client recovering from hip surgery is afraid to get out of bed. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Allow the client to remain on strict bed rest all day
options.B: Administer a double dose of strong sleeping pills
options.C: Discharge the client immediately for home recovery
options.D: Explain the risks of immobility and assist with transfer training

explanation: Encouraging early mobilization with supportive assistance prevents complications while addressing client anxiety. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h4)

question: When should prescribed analgesics ideally be given relative to physical therapy?

options.A: Two hours after therapy is completed
options.B: About thirty minutes before the session
options.D: Only at bedtime to help with sleep

explanation: Giving pain medication before therapy allows adequate time for the drug to take effect before movement begins. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h5)

question: What is the primary role of cold therapy when used in musculoskeletal rehabilitation?

options.A: Replacing the need for oral pain relievers

explanation: Applying cold constricts blood vessels, which helps minimize acute swelling and numbs localized pain. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h5)

question: Which assistive device provides the widest base of support for an unsteady client?
explanation: Walkers surround the client with a broad framework, offering maximum balance and stability. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h6)

question: A client with a weak right leg is prescribed a cane. On which side should the client hold it?
explanation: Holding the cane on the unaffected side allows the device to support the opposite weak leg during weight-bearing. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h6)

question: What is the primary indicator of successful musculoskeletal rehabilitation?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of physical exercise
options.B: Taking high doses of pain medications daily
options.C: Performing activities of daily living independently
options.D: Remaining on strict bed rest for safety

explanation: Regaining the ability to manage personal self-care tasks demonstrates true functional recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h7)

question: Why might a nurse recommend long-handled reachers to a client with hip surgery?

options.A: To cure chronic joint inflammation permanently
options.B: To replace the need for physical therapy walking
options.C: To build maximum upper arm muscle strength
options.D: To prevent bending the hip beyond safe surgical limits

explanation: Long-handled devices allow clients to pick up items without breaking hip flexion precautions. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h7)

question: Which home modification helps prevent falls for a client with mobility issues?

options.A: Placing extra furniture in narrow hallways
options.B: Polishing all wooden floors until very shiny
options.C: Turning off lights at night to save electricity
options.D: Removing loose rugs and adding bathroom grab bars

explanation: Clearing floor hazards and installing stable grab bars significantly reduces domestic fall risks. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h8)

question: Why is family involvement crucial during discharge preparation for home care?

options.A: Relatives are legally required to pay for all medical bills
options.B: Family members often serve as primary caregivers at home
options.C: Relatives take over the role of the physiotherapist
options.D: Family presence shortens the required recovery time

explanation: Involving family ensures consistent support and safe continuation of care once the client leaves the facility. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h8)
